notes: Kujo makes agent-driven engineering work inspectable, repeatable and accountable across existing workflows.
Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision. Thesis · existing agent controls acknowledged

GitHub documents agents that plan changes, edit code and review pull requests. More delegated work makes the execution record part of the review. C01 · current GitHub documentation; category context, not Kujo demand
A coupon changes a $50 cart to $50.99 instead of $45. The reviewer needs the failing test, exact change and unchanged checks. D01 · controlled checkout regression; buyer cost remains a hypothesis
The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows. T01–T14 · tool boundaries remain distinct
Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly. Composition map; not automatic end-to-end enforcement
The language, execution tools and integration adapters are inspectable in public source. T01–T14, I01–I04 · documented scope; demo tools rerun locally

A reproducible checkout regression: a coupon must preserve free shipping. The original tests fail, a one-line correction passes them. D01 · controlled fixture; driver applies correction, no autonomous-repair claim
Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary. T02–T04, T08 · tools have their own runtime dependencies
Initial buyer hypothesis: a team operating coding agents across repositories and reconstructing failures during review. Buyer, demand and willingness to pay remain unvalidated
Primary paid wedge: shared agent-run evidence and review for engineering teams. Application code stays in its existing language. No paid service or active pilot verified; proposed packaging
Illustrative revenue milestones at a proposed $500/team/month. These are active paying-team scenarios, not achieved revenue or a 24-month forecast. Enterprise revenue is excluded.
GitHub integrates agents and review. LangGraph persists workflow state. Kujo composes local execution artifacts with explicit evaluation. C01–C04 · documentation comparison; no measured superiority
Integration-led distribution: one useful repository workflow, then a buyer conversation about shared review. Proposed 30/60/90-day plan; no completed interviews or pilots claimed
Technical momentum is independently inspectable. Commercial validation is the next milestone. E01 · listing is distribution access, not customer adoption
Robert DeVore builds commercial web software and the Kujo language ecosystem. F01–F03 · third-party adoption verified; exact team-leadership scope unverified
Proposed $6M raise: a 24-month operating plan with $900K reserve. Release hiring against validation, paid pilots and retention. FIN02 · proposed terms; $30M post-money SAFE cap ≠ a priced valuation

Close on the investment thesis: $6M to commercialize Kujo’s evidence and review platform. Financing terms remain for founder confirmation; invite a diligence conversation through the existing contact route.
